name: level-ground-then-build
description: #1009: ordering `level_ground` over a rectangle of uneven ground queues excavation work for a qualified rock_digger driver instead of carving anything synchronously. For seed:42's default staffed map, the 2x2 rect (14,17)-(15,18) sits on a genuine one-voxel step (surface Y=36 at x:14, Y=35 at x:15, across both z rows) — exactly management_office tier1's own 2x2 footprint. `build management_office at:14,17` is refused first (baseline: #1008's flat-footprint rule is live), then `level_ground minX:14 maxX:15 minZ:17 maxZ:18` is ordered and drained to completion via a `pendingActionCount`-gated wait, after which the identical build order succeeds. All three of these steps click through the real BuildMenu.ts controls (`makeTerrainSection`/`armLevelGroundTool` wired a genuine drag-a-rectangle tool, mirroring the ramp tool) rather than falling back to console commands — `role: 'player'` throughout. The excavation wait is bounded to 100 ticks (the job itself completes in ~21 on this map/seed — 2 voxels plus travel) rather than a flat `tick 200`: staffed payroll (PAY_CYCLE_TICKS=10, 5 salaried employees) legitimately drains cash every pay cycle it runs through, and a needlessly long fixed pad drove cash negative before the second build's $8,000 could be charged, refusing it for insufficient funds instead of proving #1008's flat-footprint fix.

steps.description: Staffed opening (#551): 5 employees (including two driving.excavator-qualified drivers) and 4 vehicles (including one rock_digger), matching STARTING_SITE_STAFFED_COMPOSITION (balance.ts) — the same roster building-ramp-visual.json relies on for its own rock_digger work.

Staffed vehicles come unmanned (#551) — crew rock_digger #3 with driver #4, one of the two driving.excavator-qualified drivers STARTING_SITE_STAFFED_COMPOSITION grants, before ordering any excavation work. Mirrors building-ramp-visual.json's identical bootstrap step.

Baseline: the rect is genuinely uneven (Y=36 at x:14, Y=35 at x:15) so #1008's flat-footprint rule refuses the order outright, before any level_ground order exists to make this pass. Clicks through the real BuildMenu catalog + tile picker (mirrors nav-path-following-visual.json's identical uneven-footprint refusal pattern).

expect.note: Refused synchronously — no PlannedBuilding was queued for the uneven footprint.

steps.description: Order ground-levelling over the same uneven rect via the real BuildMenu control — armLevelGroundTool arms a rectangle drag exactly like armRampTool's line drag (makeTerrainSection, #1009).

expect.note: Order-time cost (2 excess voxels x LEVEL_GROUND_COST_PER_VOXEL) is charged immediately, mirroring build_ramp's own order-then-work pattern.

steps.description: Drain the queued level_ground work — a qualified rock_digger driver walks to the rect and carves the 2 excess voxels down to the lower bench. Gated on pendingActionCount reaching 0 (the level_ground action is the only one in flight at this point) rather than a flat `tick 200`: the job itself completes in ~21 ticks on this map/seed, and padding far past that needlessly burns staffed payroll (PAY_CYCLE_TICKS=10) against the second build's $8,000 below.

The identical build order that was refused before levelling now succeeds — the rect reads as flat once the level_ground action has landed. Clicks through the real BuildMenu catalog + tile picker again (mirrors building-placement-visual.json's management_office placement).

expect.note: Accepted and queued for construction — proves the flattened area now passes #1008's flat-footprint rule.
